newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa hopeful on third cellular licence in 1998.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa hopeful on third cellular licence in 1998.

text.p: South Africa is likely to grant a licence for a third cellular phone network early next year, Posts, Telecommunications and Broadcasting minister Jay Naidoo said on Tuesday.
Naidoo said the South African Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (SATRA) was conducting research for a feasibility study into the possibility of a third licence.
He added that the rapid growth shown by the country's two existing licencees meant that granting a third operating permit was likely to occur some time early in 1998.
"We are confident at this point this (the study) will allow a third operator," Naidoo told a news conference.

Naidoo was speaking at a presentation by mobile phone operator Vodacom on the firm's early fulfillment of various licence criteria involving projects aimed at creating wealth in post-apartheid South Africa.

Vodacom has more than 640,000 subscribers, giving it about 60 percent of the South African market. The industry, which is barely three years old, has already attracted more than a million phones users.

Naidoo hinted that any third licence would also involve conditions aimed at promoting the country's disadvantaged and encouraging infrastructure projects, but said the exact terms were still under discussion.
"We should learn important lessons out of the Vodacom experience," he said.
Vodacom is owned by Britain's Vodafone Plc, Rembrandt Group Ltd and Telkom. South Africa's second operator, MTN, is owned by Cable & Wireless Plc and several local groups including M-Cell Ltd.
